correctness.rationale: Any factor containing a letter transition has its cyclic run phase forced by distinct letters. Thus all interior full runs in a shared factor have equal lengths; mismatches may only be at endpoints. Every common factor embeds in the interval word between consecutive mismatches with endpoint lengths clipped to the smaller values. The interval words are common by construction. Their left predecessor and right successor disagree between sources, proving inclusion maximality. Distinct initial labels give distinct maximal words. This proves all q>=2 and positive lengths, including a single mismatch and equal-profile degeneracy. Standalone finite checker passed 2684 independent parameter pairs; it is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Four directly relevant open-access full-text primary works were compared by definitions, theorem hypotheses and implications, including the occurrence-based LMCF, circular-factor LCCF, general finite LCS and compressed RLE LCS problems. Their stated results do not subsume the closed maximal-word antichain, exact count and whole factor-language identity for this paired infinite distinct-run family. Published mathematical-result semantic searches and available historical claims yielded no direct overlap. Residual unindexed-equivalence risk is disclosed.

value.rationale: This is a complete structural classification of the intersection of two infinite periodic factor languages, not a single instance or an arbitrarily chosen parameter slice. For any number of runs and unbounded lengths, it provides all inclusion-maximal common strings, an exact formula for their number (number of mismatching run types), and a sharp common-length cutoff. A symbolic O(q)-sized run list represents what may be an exponentially large decoded factor set. It isolates mismatch-free cyclic intervals as the only way long exact matches persist, a useful invariant for compressed cyclic-string comparison.
